title: PR#52/#27: archive destination write escapes the conflict guard

Result: task both archived on disk AND still live in tasks.org, envelope falsely reports partial:false / saved_files:[]. Fix direction: match \.org\(_archive\)?\' (or track every buffer dirtied/saved in the dispatch) across preflight-org-buffers, discard-and-reload-org-buffers, revert-org-buffers and saved_files; preflight peer Org buffers for staleness even when not yet modified. title: PR#52/#27: refile saves source before destination — conflict loses the task entirely

A conflict on the destination save writes the source WITHOUT the task, then discard-and-reload reverts the destination -> task present in neither file. This is a NEW loss mode the fix introduces; pre-fix the same race clobbered the external write but kept the task. Fix direction: swap the order so destination saves first, leaving an abort duplicated (recoverable) rather than deleted. Add a regression asserting the task survives a conflict on the second save.

title: PR#53/#26: probe-exit-1 conflates stale socket with live daemon — gc/stop rmtree a RUNNING daemon

This defeats the very failure #26 exists to fix and violates the spec requirement that live pre-upgrade daemons stay visible and stoppable. ALSO: the module comment at L400-403 claims discovery works via 'socket and cmdline metadata' — no such path exists (grep cmdline matches only the comment); fix or delete it. Fix direction: probe liveness with a universally-answerable form (e.g. (emacs-pid)) before asking for daemon-info, treating 'pid answered but daemon-info errored' as live with ttl null; or discriminate on the *ERROR* stderr prefix. Add coverage for the ambiguous case — current tests only cover socket-missing.

title: #58: category headings sever task ancestry (model + CLI) — retires §7 row 13
description:
Category headings SEVER task ancestry. Implement §2's severing definition
across the reference model and the CLI, and retire §7 row 13.

Normative text is IN THIS REPO — read it, do not re-derive it:
SEMANTICS.md §2 ("Task descent (severing)"), §4.4, §4.11, §5.2, and §7 row 13.
Ruling summary: a task's parent task is its immediate parent heading iff that
heading is a task; tasks below a category heading form an independent task
world and are never task descendants of anything above it. A task whose only
children are category headings is a LEAF. Closing a task over open tasks under
its category headings is LEGAL and emits a `warnings` entry observing them
(observed fact, not an effect of the mutation).

## The piercing surface — already probed, do not re-investigate

This was enumerated and empirically confirmed on 2026-08-11 against master
e7cec5e. Work this list; verify each item rather than rediscovering it.

ALREADY CONFORMANT — leave alone (direct-children based):
  - `org-gtd-cli/has-todo-children-p` (org-gtd-cli.el:1360) filters on
    `(= (org-current-level) child-level)`. Backs `show`'s `is_project`,
    `projects`, `subtasks`. Verified: `show` over a severed child already
    reports `is_project: false` and `projects` correctly omits it.
  - `org-gtd-cli/subproject-all-done-p` (org-gtd-cli.el:3311) and
    `org-gtd-cli/first-promotable-child` (org-gtd-cli.el:3330).

PIERCES — the actual work:

1. THE I4 CLOSURE GUARD IS NOT CLI CODE. `+gtd-core.el:72` sets
   `org-enforce-todo-dependencies t`, delegating to org's own blocker, which
   walks the whole subtree. `org-gtd-cli/reject-blocked-close`
   (org-gtd-cli.el:3894) only FORMATS the rejection — its docstring already
   reserves this slot ("so #58's row-13 fix lands once"). Fixing this means
   narrowing or overriding org's blocker (e.g. an `org-blocker-hook` entry),
   NOT editing a predicate. Budget for this being the largest piece.
   CONFIRMED REPRO:
     * TODO Home
     ** TODO Renovate the bathroom
     *** Plumbing
     **** TODO Call plumber
     **** DONE Measure
   `set-done "Renovate the bathroom"` is REJECTED today, org naming the
   severed "Call plumber" as blocker. Under §2 it must SUCCEED and emit a
   §4.4 `warnings` entry observing the open severed task.

2. `gtd/is-project-p` (+gtd-core.el:102) — subtree-wide
   `re-search-forward "^\*+ "`. Backs §4.5's leaf-vs-subproject branch.
   CONFIRMED REPRO: with
     * TODO Home
     ** TODO Fix the porch light
     ** TODO Renovate the bathroom
     *** Plumbing
     **** TODO Call plumber
   `set-done "Fix the porch light"` yields NO promotion and NO notice
   (`side_effects: []`). Under §2, "Renovate the bathroom" is a LEAF and must
   be promoted TODO->NEXT by the §4.5 scan.

3. `gtd/is-task-p` (+gtd-core.el:118) — same subtree-wide loop, inverse result.

4. `gtd/is-subproject-p` (+gtd-core.el:134) and `gtd/find-project-task`
   (+gtd-core.el:156) — walk UP via `org-up-heading-safe`, skipping past
   category headings to a task above. Must stop at the first category heading.

5. `gtd/has-active-in-subtree-p` (+gtd-core.el:172) — subtree-wide NEXT/WAITING
   regex.

6. `gtd/skip-stuck-projects` (+gtd-core.el:406) and
   `gtd/skip-non-stuck-projects` (+gtd-core.el:426) — pierce twice: they call
   `gtd/is-project-p` AND run their own subtree-wide
   `re-search-forward "^\*+ NEXT "`.

Items 2-6 live in `+gtd-core.el`, the file the interactive Emacs config also
loads, so this change reaches `agenda-view` and interactive Emacs together.
That is intended.

## Scope

1. Reference model (`gtd_reference_model.py`): `task_descendants`, `is_project`,
   `active()` and any other traversal stop at category headings. Update tier-1
   generator assumptions about keyword-less nodes inside projects. The §4.5
   scan's direct-children reading becomes correct by definition; retire the
   PARKED comment at the scan site.
2. CLI + shared core: implement severing across the six piercing items above.
3. Add the §4.4 close warning over open severed tasks.
4. Correct `org-gtd-cli/subproject-all-done-p`'s docstring, which currently
   claims §4.5 "does not pin whether tasks below the subproject's own category
   headings count (§2 severing — PARKED, awaiting a ruling)". §2 DOES pin it
   and the predicate is already conformant; there is no open ruling.
5. Delete §7 row 13 and its inline `*Divergence…*` markers when green.

OUT OF SCOPE: `delete`. SEMANTICS.md §4.12 states the delete guard is
"deliberately structural, not semantic: §2's severing never widens what delete
may destroy". That still holds — do NOT make delete severing-aware. (Its
surrounding sentence reads as half-true since delete also gained a semantic
blocker guard; that is a prose wart, not licence to change behaviour.)

## Acceptance criteria

- Both confirmed repros above now behave per §2: the close succeeds with a
  warnings entry; the severed-leaf shape is promoted TODO->NEXT.
- Model and CLI agree on severing across the whole probed surface — tier-2
  conformance green with the piercing divergence flags removed.
- A project with real direct task children keeps its behaviour unchanged
  (regression: "Renovate the kitchen" with DONE direct children and a severed
  "Book electrician" still reports project-needs-review correctly).
- `delete`'s behaviour is unchanged.
- §7 row 13 and its markers deleted.
- Model moves in the SAME commit as the CLI, or conformance breaks.

## Verification

  nix develop --command python3 -m pytest -q -n 4
  ORG_GTD_TEST_PROFILE=thorough nix develop --command python3 -m pytest -q -n 4
  nix flake check
  nix build .#org-gtd-cli

Then exercise the BUILT binary (`result/bin/org-gtd-cli`) against
`dev-data/real/` and `dev-data/degenerate/`, including both repros above.
`nix flake check` builds COMMITTED sources only — commit first.

Closes #58.

title: #56: closure repair cascade + WAITING keyword-outgrown repair — retires §7 rows 10-11
description:
Implement the two §4.0 repair conventions — closure repair (the reopen
cascade) and the WAITING keyword-outgrown repair. Retires §7 rows 10 and 11.

Normative text is IN THIS REPO — read it, do not re-derive it: SEMANTICS.md
§4.0 (both repair paragraphs), §4.3, §4.6 (WAITING exit cleanup), §4.7, §4.8,
and §7 rows 10-11.

## Scope

1. CLOSURE REPAIR (reopen cascade). Any operation that places or reveals an
   OPEN task in the task descent of a CLOSED ancestor reopens that ancestor
   chain — each closed ancestor becomes TODO, each reported as a
   `state-change` side effect. I4 stays a hard invariant; arrival makes the
   record live again. Four triggers, all of which must work:
     - `add-subtask` with an open state under a closed heading
     - `set-state` reopening a task below closed ancestors
     - `refile` of an open subtree into a closed destination chain
     - `set-next` on a closed PROJECT-CHILD leaf: today rejected outright,
       becomes accept-and-reopen straight to NEXT via the same cascade.
       A closed LONE task stays rejected (I3). §4.7 is normative and precise
       on this distinction; follow §4.7, not §4.0's shorter phrasing.

   IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT: walk task descent via the reference model's
   `task_descendants` notion — do NOT open-code a subtree traversal. A sibling
   bead in this epic changes what "task descent" means (category headings sever
   ancestry); a cascade built on the shared helper inherits that automatically,
   an open-coded one silently diverges.

2. WAITING KEYWORD-OUTGROWN REPAIR. A WAITING leaf gaining its first direct
   task child (via `add-subtask` or `refile`) demotes WAITING->TODO in the same
   mutation. THIS EMITS UP TO THREE SIDE EFFECTS, not two — the demotion is a
   CLI-driven exit from WAITING, so the §4.6 WAITING exit cleanup runs as part
   of it:
     a. `state-change` — WAITING -> TODO on the parent.
     b. `blocker-link-removed` — one per unwound link, WHEN the demoted parent
        carried a `BLOCKER` property: `:REASON:` removed and the
        `TRIGGER`/`BLOCKER` pair unwound. The LOGBOOK record is left alone (I10).
     c. `project-needs-review` — for the demoted parent.

   DO NOT REIMPLEMENT THE CLEANUP. Call `org-gtd-cli/waiting-exit-cleanup`
   (org-gtd-cli.el:3628). Its docstring already names this work: "Callable from
   every WAITING exit site, so #56's keyword-outgrown demotion wires in without
   duplication." It supports `--dry-run` parity through its DRY argument.

   The NEXT variant of this repair already exists; the review-flag addition is
   WAITING-specific.

3. Zone placement of any repaired/demoted task follows §4.1: a demoted NEXT
   moves to just below the NEXT prefix; a demoted WAITING keeps its position.
   Placement is NEVER a side effect (§4.0).

## Files involved

- `org-gtd-cli.el` — the mutation paths above.
- `gtd_reference_model.py` — drop the divergence routing for these behaviours.
- `test_gtd_model_properties.py` — retire the I4-outside-closure and
  WAITING-leaf entries from the parked-gap predicate.
- `test_gtd_conformance.py` — add/flip the row-10 and row-11 witnesses.
- `SEMANTICS.md` — delete §7 rows 10-11 and their inline markers when green.
- `+gtd-core.el` mirror is NOT this repo's scope (tracked separately).

## Acceptance criteria

- All four closure-repair triggers produce the reopen cascade with correct
  `side_effects`; `set-next` on a closed project-child leaf succeeds and
  reopens to NEXT; a closed LONE task is still rejected.
- A WAITING parent carrying a `BLOCKER` link, demoted by `add-subtask` or
  `refile`, ends with no `:REASON:` and no `BLOCKER` property, and the
  blocker's `TRIGGER` entry no longer names it.
- That demotion reports all three side effects. A WAITING parent with a reason
  but NO blocker link reports `state-change` + `project-needs-review` only —
  no spurious `blocker-link-removed`.
- `--dry-run` predicts the same effect set the real mutation produces.
- Tier-1 gap-predicate entries for these families are retired; tier-2 witnesses
  green in normative mode; §7 rows 10-11 deleted.

## Verification

  nix develop --command python3 -m pytest -q -n 4
  ORG_GTD_TEST_PROFILE=thorough nix develop --command python3 -m pytest -q -n 4
  nix flake check
  nix build .#org-gtd-cli

Then exercise the BUILT binary (`result/bin/org-gtd-cli`) against

carries a blocker link. `nix flake check` builds COMMITTED sources only.

Closes #56.

title: #57: refile --to unique-or-error + refile side-effect reporting — retires §7 row 12
description:
Make `refile --to` unique-or-error, and make refile report its repairs as
side effects. Retires §7 row 12.

Normative text is IN THIS REPO — read it, do not re-derive it: SEMANTICS.md
§4.0 (destination addressing + the side-effect vocabulary), §4.8, and §7
row 12.

DEPENDS ON THE REPAIR-FAMILY BEAD IN THIS EPIC. Part 2 below reports repairs
that bead implements; it cannot be completed before that one lands. Part 1 is
independent of it.

## Scope

1. `refile --to` BECOMES UNIQUE-OR-ERROR. Today it resolves by first match in
   document order and is silent on duplicates. Duplicate exact-match
   destinations become an error reporting the candidates — I12 applied to
   destinations exactly as to targets. Nothing is mutated on the error path.
   Unique destinations resolve as before. Matching stays case-insensitive
   EXACT over headings of any kind, category headings included, self-nesting
   excluded (§4.0).

2. REFILE REPORTS ITS REPAIRS AS SIDE EFFECTS. Today it reports none. Every
   repair refile performs is reported with the same vocabulary the primitive
   commands use (§4.0: same vocabulary for the same repair). That includes:
     - `state-change` for a moved NEXT demoted to TODO (freestanding or
       duplicate-NEXT sibling),
     - `state-change` for each reopened ancestor in a closure cascade,
     - `state-change` + `project-needs-review` for a demoted WAITING target
       parent,
     - `blocker-link-removed` — one per unwound link — when that demoted
       WAITING parent carried a `BLOCKER` property. §4.8 lets refile trigger
       the WAITING-parent demotion, and §4.6 makes that demotion run the
       WAITING exit cleanup, so refile MUST be able to emit this. Same shape
       the primitive commands and §4.12's waiting-side delete unwind produce.

   BOUNDARY: zone placement and reorder are NEVER side effects, in refile as
   everywhere (§4.0/§4.1). Placement is presentation, not a state change.

## Files involved

- `org-gtd-cli.el` — refile destination resolution + the response envelope.
- `gtd_reference_model.py` — drop first-hit modelling if present; align
  reporting.
- `test_gtd_conformance.py` — the row-12 witness.
- `SEMANTICS.md` — delete §7 row 12 and its markers when green.

## Acceptance criteria

- Duplicate `--to` destinations error WITHOUT mutating, and the error names
  the candidates; unique ones resolve exactly as before.
- Refile's `side_effects` match the reference model's prediction exactly in
  tier-2 conformance.
- Refiling a subtree under a WAITING parent that carries a blocker link
  reports `blocker-link-removed`.
- No placement or reorder appears in `side_effects`.
- §7 row 12 deleted.

## Verification

  nix develop --command python3 -m pytest -q -n 4
  ORG_GTD_TEST_PROFILE=thorough nix develop --command python3 -m pytest -q -n 4
  nix flake check
  nix build .#org-gtd-cli

Then exercise the BUILT binary (`result/bin/org-gtd-cli`) against
`dev-data/real/` and `dev-data/degenerate/` — at minimum a duplicate-`--to`
rejection and a refile that triggers a reported repair. `nix flake check`
builds COMMITTED sources only.

Closes #57.
